title: Batching Spectra Pilot - Weekly Review
summary: Weekly POC sync to review throughput numbers after the last retune. Team discussed batch size distribution, observed queue jitter during 95th percentile traffic spikes, and tradeoffs between steady-state batching and stricter concurrency caps. Action items: run a batch-profile with finer buckets, test a lower concurrency cap with prefix KV caching enabled, and provide an updated dashboard link. Agreed next check-in in 1 week unless telemetry requires earlier triage.
action_items: Diego Ramos: run batch_profile with 5ms/10ms/20ms buckets and attach CSV to the pilot folder (due 2027-07-02)
Aisha Patel: instrument a synthetic steady-state traffic job to reproduce the 95th percentile spike and share logs (due 2027-07-01)
Maya Chen: send trimmed pricing estimate for sustained Dedicated capacity and note fallback model tiers (due 2027-07-03)
next_steps: Diego to post batch histograms + histogram-based suggestion in pilot slack
StratusGrid to run a 2-hour synthetic run during their off-peak to capture queue jitter
Maya to schedule optional triage if 95th pctl latency remains > 420ms
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-30
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Aisha (StratusGrid), Marcus (Infra), Nora (PM)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick agenda: throughput numbers from last week, a few retunes we pushed, and decide next steps for the steady-state run. um, Diego do you want to lead the numbers?
[00:23] Diego (Redwood SE): yeah, sure. so we pulled the telemetry from the pilot run that ended yesterday. steady requests per second averaged 820 rps, token throughput looked fine, but we saw queue depth spikes up to 120 when a burst hit the front end. the continuous batching algorithm packed well in steady state but struggled when the arrival distribution had heavy tails.
[00:46] Aisha (StratusGrid): can you clarify "heavy tails" there? is that coming from our experimental client retry logic? we did push a change last week.
[01:10] Diego: possibly. we saw a cluster of concurrent requests originating from the same lambda pool; retries amplified burstiness. also KV cache hit rate dipped from 84% to about 64% during the spike which increased per-token compute. kay-vee cache was referenced as "k-v cache" in the logs, sometimes mis-cased by the ingest pipeline.
[01:38] Marcus (Infra): yeah that lambda test could be it. we can run the synthetic job Aisha mentioned to replicate. the 95th percentile latency during the spike was ~450ms, which is above your target SLA of 400ms.
[02:02] Nora (PM): just to be explicit — our success criteria is mean latency < 200ms, p95 < 400ms, and costs within the quoted committed range. if p95 stays above that we need a fallback plan.
[02:28] Maya: right. fallback options are: tighten concurrency (limit inflight per connection), accept larger batch sizes but longer tail latency, or route burst traffic to a higher-capacity model variant. Diego, what did the experimentation show?
[02:49] Diego: i ran a quick sweep: concurrency cap at 24 gave best p95 but reduced overall throughput by ~8%. increasing batching window to 25ms improved token efficiency but pushed p95 up in bursts. continuous batching is good for average-case but we need queue shaping for tails.
[03:15] Aisha: so if we cap concurrency are we risking higher cost per token? what's the tradeoff again?
[03:31] Diego: yeah there's a cost/latency trade. with lower concurrency we have shorter queues so p95 drops but GPU utilization also drops slightly which raises cost per token. we can offset that with kv cache hits — if the cache hit goes up to 90% the economics look favorable.
[03:55] Marcus: what's our current cache configuration? are we priming prefixes?
[04:10] Diego: we're doing prefix caching for 60% of calls; prefix length and priming cadence may need adjustment. one idea: pre-warm the kv cache for high-frequency routes during expected peaks.
[04:28] Nora: pre-warm sounds operationally heavy. can we do adaptive pre-warm based on request histograms?
[04:44] Diego: yes, we can import a short-term hot-key detector into the routing layer, low-cost.
[05:01] Maya: practical ask — can we get batch histograms in more granular buckets? last CSV had 50ms bins which masks micro-batching behavior.
[05:16] Diego: absolutely. i'll run batch_profile with 5ms and 10ms buckets and share the CSV.
[05:27] Aisha: perfect. also i want to understand jitter in queue depth. is that instrumentation we need to add or is it already present?
[05:40] Diego: we have queue depth metrics per host but not aggregated to route-level histograms. i'll add that for the next run.
[05:52] Aisha: ok. on the synthetic run — we'll spin up a replay that mirrors last week's traffic plus the lambda retry pattern. goal is to reproduce that 95th pctl event in a controlled window.
[06:08] Marcus: note — during that window our autoscaler also kicked, which creates a temporary imbalance. autoscaler cooldowns may be exacerbating jitter.
[06:25] Maya: good call. can you capture scaler events in the same trace, Marcus?
[06:33] Marcus: yes we'll include scaler timestamps.
[06:39] Nora: any quick wins we can apply today?
[06:44] Diego: a small one: enable a soft concurrency cap per route, e.g., soft 32 with fast-fail to fallback tier when queue exceeds threshold. it reduces tail significantly with modest throughput impact.
[06:58] Aisha: what's fast-fail? do we lose user requests?
[07:04] Diego: not lose — degrade to a cheaper, faster model with slightly reduced quality, it's an explicit fallback we discussed previously. we can surface reasons in response metadata.
[07:19] Maya: customers often prefer transparent fallbacks rather than long waits. okay next — telemetry link. did you upload the dashboard snapshot?
[07:30] Diego: yes, i posted a dashboard link in the pilot folder and the slack channel; i'll include a trimmed permalink in the follow-up note.
[07:42] Aisha: i saw the dashboard. curious about a spike at 14:17 UTC, looks like a correlated external job.
[07:52] Diego: that timing matches your lambda experiment.
[07:58] Nora: cost question: if we use Dedicated for steady-state but rely on Hosted fallback for bursts, how does billing look?
[08:10] Maya: typically Dedicated provides committed capacity pricing; fallback to hosted is billed versioned to the account and we can provide blended estimates. i'll share a short pricing sketch in the follow-up.
[08:25] Aisha: can you also call out model tiers and quantization options? those affect both latency and cost.
[08:33] Maya: yes, i'll annotate with recommended quant profiles and the expected p50/p95 tradeoffs per tier.
[08:40] Marcus: any security concerns with routing to hosted fallback? data residency?
[08:46] Maya: good point. for PII-sensitive routes we can avoid hosted fallback; that's a route-level policy. we'll mark those routes as private-only.
[08:57] Nora: ok. timeline wise, we want to decide on a steady state config by next week's sync so we can start ramping capacity the following week.
[09:07] Maya: agreed. so action items recap: Diego runs finer batch_profile, StratusGrid runs synthetic replay, Marcus collects scaler traces, Maya shares pricing and fallback notes.
[09:23] Aisha: quick clarification — what concurrency cap did you say reduced p95 the most?
[09:28] Diego: around 24 inflight per model instance in our tests. but let's validate with the new histograms.
[09:36] Nora: can we run a short A/B on canary with soft cap 24 vs baseline 40?
[09:42] Diego: yep we can do a canary with traffic split 10/90 and run for an hour. i'll prepare a playbook.
[09:52] Maya: timeline — can Diego post the batch histograms by Friday?
[09:56] Diego: yes, i'll have them by EOD Friday (2027-07-02).
[10:02] Aisha: StratusGrid will run the synthetic replay on Thursday night to avoid peak. results posted Friday morning.
[10:10] Marcus: we'll attach scaler logs to the same thread.
[10:15] Maya: anything else?
[10:20] Aisha: one micro request — when Diego posts histograms, include a small note about observed micro-batching behaviour with prefix lengths, so we can see where priming helps.
[10:31] Diego: will do.
[10:35] Maya: great. we'll reconvene same time next week unless an earlier triage is needed. thanks everyone.
[10:42] (end)
